title: How Does Property Development Finance Work in Scotland?
h1: How Does Property Development Finance Work in Scotland? (search-result title; H1 not separately confirmed)
summary: Blog article (not a case study) presenting property development finance as a common funding route for developers in Scotland, while noting that Scotland's unique market conditions and planning regulations should be considered. The visible content is a typology of the main finance types available: senior development loans (covering a percentage of land purchase and construction costs, typically up to 65-75% of Gross Development Value), mezzanine finance (a secondary loan that sits behind senior debt, reducing the developer's equity requirement), bridging loans, stretched senior loans and joint venture finance. The concrete guidance revealed on applying is that the lender will want a clear business case including cost estimates, projected timelines and an exit strategy. The full article body (introduction, section headings, rates, worked examples, Scottish legal specifics such as Standard Security, FAQ, calls to action) was not exposed by the search snippets.

The WebSearch tool returns paraphrased summaries of snippets rather than raw snippet text, so the 'verbatim' entries tagged [a]/[b] are the tool's wording of the excerpt, not guaranteed page wording; the two [seed] entries are the quoted sentences recorded in the first harvest pass and are consistent with the new results. Meta description, H1 (as distinct from title), section headings, FAQ, calls to action, author, publication date and any rates/worked examples were NOT revealed; metaDescription is therefore omitted and faq/ctas are empty. Search (a) also surfaced unrelated third-party pages (Scottish Business News, Greenwood Capital, Anglo Scottish Finance, Evolve Finance, FD Commercial, Fox Davidson, Together Money, RBS) carrying Scottish-specific points (Standard Security registration, 6-24 or 12-30 month terms, ~0.80%-1.30%/month rates); these are NOT Silver Oak content and are deliberately excluded from the fields above. Search (b) also returned unrelated Wikipedia pages (The KLIN Group, Silverburn Shopping Centre, Simply UK), ignored. Other Silver Oak page titles observed: 'Property Development Finance', 'Silver Oak Capital Case Studies', 'Silver Oak Capital - Commercial Mortgage Broker & Property Development Finance Solutions' (home), 'Property Conversion Finance UK', 'Senior Development Finance UK', 'Development Finance Brokers - Get a Instant Quote Now' (the last shows a 'Get a Instant Quote Now' CTA on a different page, not confirmed on this article). Confidence is medium because the typology and the 65-75% GDV figure are triple-corroborated, but the bulk of the article body remains unseen.
